one_liner: Incremental 3-D k-d tree for LiDAR SLAM maps: point/box updates without full rebuilds; per-scan time 1.03-2.1x below nanoflann and Boost R*-tree.
what_it_does: ikd-Tree keeps a k-d tree over a growing, moving 3-D point map: you Build() once, then Add_Points (with optional on-tree voxel downsampling), Delete_Points, Delete_Point_Boxes and Add_Point_Boxes as the robot moves, and query with Nearest_Search (k-NN with an optional max distance), Box_Search and Radius_Search. It is a templated class KD_TREE<PointType> whose points must expose float x, y, z members; the .cpp explicitly instantiates it for its own point type, pcl::PointXYZ and pcl::PointXYZI. It is not a drop-in for nanoflann, Boost.Geometry's rtree or PCL's octree; it has its own API built around PCL-style point vectors.
how_it_is_fast: Each node stores its subtree's bounding cuboid, size and lazy 'deleted' labels, so box deletes and box re-adds mark whole subtrees in O(log n)-style traversals and push labels down later instead of touching every point. Points are inserted one at a time, and a subtree is rebuilt only when it violates an alpha-balanced criterion (child share outside 1-alpha_bal..alpha_bal) or an alpha-deleted criterion (invalid share above alpha_del), a scapegoat-tree style partial rebuild. Subtrees of 1,500 points or more are rebuilt on a second pthread while the main thread keeps updating and querying; updates made meanwhile go into an operation log that is replayed onto the new subtree before it is swapped in. k-NN uses bounding-box ('bounds-overlap-ball') pruning plus the max-distance cutoff that LiDAR odometry naturally supplies.
when_to_use: LiDAR or LiDAR-inertial odometry and mapping that inserts a few thousand downsampled points per scan and runs small k-NN (FAST-LIO2 uses k=5) against a local map of 10^5-10^6 points
Sliding-window or moving-map applications that need box-wise deletion of everything outside a region, which ikd-Tree does with lazy labels instead of per-point removes

Real-time loops where worst-case update latency matters more than mean: in FAST-LIO2's Table III ikd-Tree's update peak stays at or under 214 ms while nanoflann's dynamic index peaks above 3 s on seven sequences
Embedded x86 or ARM Linux robots already using PCL (the paper runs FAST-LIO2 on an i7-8550U and on a Cortex-A73 board)
when_not_to_use: Anything other than 3-D float points: x/y/z and per-axis node ranges are hard-coded (issue #26 asks about 2-D; issue #39 reports pcl::PointXYZL not working)
Bulk loading or large batch inserts: Add_Points inserts point by point, and issue #36 reports 30,000-point inserts slower than PCL's kd-tree
Commercial or permissive-license projects: GPLv2, and the README asks commercial users to contact the authors
Code that needs a maintained dependency or exact deletes: last commit 2022-03-04, 24 open issues, including an open report (#25) that ties on the split coordinate make point lookups miss
Pure insert-heavy workloads: in FAST-LIO2's comparison PCL's octree has the fastest incremental updates in most sequences; ikd-Tree wins on k-NN and total time

integration.form: source-drop (ikd-Tree/ikd_Tree.h + ikd_Tree.cpp; FAST-LIO2 vendors its own copy)
integration.dependencies: PCL (the header includes pcl/point_types.h; Eigen::aligned_allocator arrives through it), POSIX threads (pthread, usleep). The demos need PCL 1.8+
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 (the demo CMakeLists builds with -std=c++14 -pthread -O3); CMake 2.8+
integration.platforms: POSIX/Linux (pthread and unistd.h); Windows and macOS not documented
integration.thread_safety: Not documented in the README. Internally each tree runs its own rebuild thread synchronised with mutexes, and the FAST-LIO2 paper says k-NN supports multi-threaded search, but issue #20 reports a double free when Nearest_Search is called from several OpenMP threads (closed, no fix shown). Treat updates as single-writer

gotchas: Each KD_TREE object embeds a 1,000,000-entry operation-log ring buffer (MANUAL_Q, Q_LEN) by value, about 44 MB per tree for its own point type and about 64 MB for pcl::PointXYZI (derived from the header's struct layout), so construct it on the heap (KD_TREE::Ptr). The ring buffer's push has no overflow check, so more than 10^6 operations logged during one background rebuild would silently overwrite entries

Deletes are lazy: deleted points stay in memory and in tree size until a rebuild, so memory and k-NN cost depend on rebuild timing (issue #42 reports memory not released after deleting the root). Delete_by_point descends one side only on strict less-than, which is why issue #25's tie case can miss a point

The constructor starts a pthread and prints 'Multi thread started' to stdout; the destructor joins it (issue #43 reports a hang on destruction). Default parameters differ between the constructor (balance 0.6) and InitializeKDTree (balance 0.7)

Only ikdTree_PointType, pcl::PointXYZ and pcl::PointXYZI are explicitly instantiated in ikd_Tree.cpp; other point types need an added 'template class' line (issue #30 reports an undefined reference to KD_TREE<POINT_TYPE>::~KD_TREE(), the symptom of a missing instantiation)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ikd-Tree over nanoflann's dynamic index when you need bounded worst-case update latency, box deletion and on-tree downsampling for a single 3-D LiDAR map; nanoflann is BSD, header-only, any dimension and maintained. Pick PSI/SpaceTreeLib or Pkd-tree instead for large parallel batch updates on many-core servers, and PH-tree for a permissively licensed dynamic index with general key types.
verified_claims_summary: In the peer-reviewed FAST-LIO2 paper (IEEE T-RO 2022, same group), the authors wired ikd-Tree, Boost.Geometry's R*-tree, PCL's octree and nanoflann's dynamic k-d tree into FAST-LIO2 and timed 18 sequences on an Intel i7-8550U (DJI Manifold 2-C), k=5, compiler not stated. Total per-scan time (updates plus kNN) was 1.03-1.34x lower than nanoflann, 1.26-2.09x lower than the R*-tree and 2.29-3.06x lower than the octree (derived from page data). The octree had the fastest updates in most sequences, and the main win over nanoflann is avoiding its multi-second update peaks. The baseline integration code (with emulated downsampling for the other trees) is not public.
status_note: Abandoned since 2022-03-04 (24 open issues, several crash and correctness reports unanswered) and GPLv2-only, so vendor it knowingly; the copy inside FAST-LIO2 is the best-exercised version.
